body:
So yes to do so maybe the best option would be to:
1. create one instantsearch per tab
2. each instantsearch has his own searchbox
3. show/hide the corresponding searchbox based on the selected tab
4. show/hide the corresponding widgets based on the selected tab (from what I see, the widgets will be different: no price slider for news)
5. create a [custom widget](https://community.algolia.com/instantsearch.js/documentation/#custom-widgets) that you add to every instance of instantsearch and that will update the counts next to each tab
6. create a custom widget that you add to every instance of instantsearch and that will update the query (helper.setQuery) every time the widget goes from hidden/shown then redo a search to update the interface (helper.search())
6. on tab change, show the right widgets, update the query (instance.helper.setQuery)

This is rather complex but what you are trying to do is very advanced and requires this coding. Let me know what you think
